% Define the transformation

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Exactly one colour per cell
1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

% -------------------------------------------------------------
% Transformation rules

% Keep the original colour of every non‑zero cell
output(R,C,X) :- input(R,C,X), X != 0.

% Leading zero block (the zeros left of the first non‑zero) become colour 4
output(R,C,4) :- input(R,C,0), leading_zero(R,C).

% All other zero cells stay zero
output(R,C,0) :- input(R,C,0), not leading_zero(R,C).

% -------------------------------------------------------------
% Constraints – forbid any colour other than the one we intend

% Non‑zero cells must keep their colour
:- output(R,C,Y), input(R,C,X), X != 0, Y != X.

% Leading zeros may only be colour 4
:- output(R,C,Y), input(R,C,0), leading_zero(R,C), Y != 4.

% Other zeros may only be colour 0
:- output(R,C,Y), input(R,C,0), not leading_zero(R,C), Y != 0.

% -------------------------------------------------------------
% Leading‑zero predicate

leading_zero(R,C) :-
    row(R), col(C),
    input(R,C,0),
    not has_nonzero_left(R,C),
    exists_nonzero_right_gap(R,C).

has_nonzero_left(R,C) :-
    row(R), col(D), D < C,
    input(R,D,Color), Color != 0.

has_nonzero_between(R,C,Cp) :-
    row(R), col(K), K > C, K < Cp,
    input(R,K,Color), Color != 0.

exists_nonzero_right_gap(R,C) :-
    row(R), col(Cp), col(C), Cp > C,
    input(R,Cp,Color), Color != 0,
    not has_nonzero_between(R,C,Cp).

#show output/3.
</asp>

% --------------------------------------------------------------

% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Exactly one colour per cell
1 { output(R,C,Col) : color(Col) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

% Flanked detection (two orientations)
flanked(R,C,X) :-
    row(R), col(C),
    input(R,CL,X), col(CL), CL < C,
    input(R,CR,X), col(CR), CR > C.

flanked2(R,C,X) :-
    row(R), col(C),
    input(R,CL,X), col(CL), CL > C,
    input(R,CR,X), col(CR), CR < C.

flanked(R,C,X) :- flanked(R,C,X), flanked2(R,C,X).

% Transformation mapping
transform(8,4).
transform(3,6).
transform(6,3).
transform(4,2).
transform(2,8).

% At most one flanking colour per cell
:- flanked(R,C,X), flanked(R,C,Y), X != Y.

% Anchor cells (flanked and same colour): keep original colour
:- output(R,C,Y), flanked(R,C,X), input(R,C,X), Y != X.

% Flanked non‑anchor cells: must become transformed colour

% Non‑flanked non‑zero cells: keep original colour

% Non‑flanked zeros: stay zero
:- output(R,C,Y), input(R,C,0), not flanked(R,C,0), Y != 0.
